title: The Number That Comes Up
logline: A lottery-ticket seller calls to the passing crowd all day, while regulars buy the same numbers morning after morning, certain today might finally be the day.
human_question: What does it mean to want the same thing every day, without ever quite expecting to get it?

situation.what_happens: A ticket seller works a fixed pitch from morning to night, calling out to everyone who passes. Some customers buy without breaking stride and without a word, the same numbers as always. Others are talked into a first ticket by the calling itself. In the evening the draw is read out and almost everybody loses, which everybody already knew. The next morning is the same morning again.
situation.who_is_involved: A seller whose whole income is a commission on small sales; regulars who buy daily out of habit; occasional buyers talked into one; the households behind both sides of the counter. The seller is the practised, unexcited half of every exchange and the buyer the hopeful half, which is the same pairing as a dealer appraising, flat-eyed, a stone a family has carried a long way in hope.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the buyers, a small sum daily set against a change of life that will not come, and in some of them a habit that costs more than they say it does. For the seller, a living made out of other people's hope and their own knowledge of the odds. For the film, the ease of sneering at poor buyers, which would sink it.
situation.how_it_unfolds: The day has a fixed shape, a slow morning, a rush, an evening draw and a clean start tomorrow, while the season around it has none: a rare win somewhere nearby changes the trade for a week. Over months a regular may stop, or double down, or the seller may lose the pitch altogether. What happens at any evening's draw is decided by the draw.

concept_merge.why_together: C006 contributes the three dials the sources set on wanting: joy or flat feeling, with or without a story that justifies it, and rising sharply on its own or needing a push from outside, a seller's calling being the plainest prompt there is. C004 contributes the frame in which these arise, the ordinary sense-sphere day of sight, sound and small transaction, and the definition of greed as an attaching that never comes with displeasure.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Together they show a form of wanting with no excitement in it at all, which is the hardest kind to recognise as wanting. The sources go further and rank the flat, unexcited version as stronger than the joyful one; the digest records that ranking as unexplained and needing an expert check, so the film can let a viewer notice the flatness without asserting the ranking. The same flatness sits on the seller's side of the counter: wherever somebody hoping meets somebody practised, the practised one is not less involved, only quieter.

concept_links.why: A seller's calling is prompting made audible, while regulars buy unprompted and out of habit; the sources separate wanting that arises sharply of its own accord from wanting urged on by others or by oneself, and sort it again by joyful or flat feeling [C006-M:L5] [C006-P:L44] [C006-P:L74]. The sources also rank flat wanting above joyful, which the digest flags as unexplained and needing an expert check [C006-M:L19], so the film may show the flatness but must not assert the ranking.

The ticket seller is one of the digest's own story seeds, a reaching for a hoped-for good inside an ordinary sense-sphere day [C004-P:L25], with delight on one face and flat routine on another [C004-M:L17]. The digest is explicit that one source's remarks on gambling belong to that author's own contemporary moral commentary rather than to the teaching [C004-P:L57], and the film must not carry them.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Wanting does not always feel exciting. Buying the same numbers every morning can be a flat, habitual reach, and a newcomer may buy only because somebody kept calling, and both are the same wanting.
what_must_be_real: The seller's real trade, the regulars' real habits, and their own words about why they play. No win or loss arranged, and no purchase prompted for the film.
position_hint: middle, late: the group's clearest picture of wanting without joy, placed just before wanting starts meeting refusal.
risks: Sneering at poor buyers or at the seller's trade
Turning gambling into a moral lesson, which the digest sets outside the teaching
Privacy of regulars who may not want a habit shown
Asserting the sources' ranking of flat wanting over joyful, which the digest flags for expert check
drop_if: No seller or regulars will speak honestly about the habit
The habit can only be shown by exposing someone who did not understand what they agreed to

connections.note: Hope bought in small daily doses here, hope refused all at once there.
Folded in: the practised, unexcited side of a hopeful exchange, and the sources' surprising ranking of flat wanting above joyful.

selection.reason: The group's picture of joyless, habitual wanting, now carrying the appraiser-and-hoper contrast folded in from IDEA-0015.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
